relations.name: completion_events
relations.role: The completion funnel's event log. Records which SURFACE a completion was claimed from.
relations.summary: Migrated to app.completion_events, but two readiness conflicts block it: the source value domain (4.1) and the required game_id FK (4.2).

columns.name: id
columns.note: Coordinator ruling: preserve source event IDs. Without the retained uuid the funnel cannot be reconciled against pre-cutover analytics.
columns.transform: uuid -> bigint identity, with the legacy uuid retained so the source event ID survives.

columns.name: user_id
columns.note: NOT NULL in both.
columns.transform: uuid -> integer via migration.account_map.

columns.name: game_id
columns.note: readiness 4.2. Legacy is NULLABLE with NO foreign key; v2 requires game_id integer NOT NULL references catalog.games(id) (M1:408). Resolution order: library_row_map on game_id, then game_map on steam_appid. An event with neither is UNMIGRATABLE as-is, yet plan section 3 requires user history to survive losing ownership. Coordinator ruling: preserve unknown-game history. Proposal: a sentinel catalog.games row is NOT acceptable (it fabricates a game); instead relax to a nullable game_id in a new M3 migration, or archive the unresolvable events with their steam_appid.
columns.transform: resolution order is migration.library_row_map on game_id, then migration.game_map on steam_appid. An event that resolves loads into app.completion_events. An event with neither identifier loads into app.unknown_completion_history with its original nullable identifiers intact, so history survives losing ownership without fabricating a catalogue row. app.completion_event_registry records which relation holds each legacy_event_id.

columns.name: steam_appid
columns.note: Nullable in legacy, so it is a fallback and not a guarantee. Its presence or absence is exactly what probe P07g measures.
columns.transform: The fallback resolution path when game_id is null or unresolvable. bigint appid -> catalog.games.id.

columns.name: source
columns.note: readiness 4.1. Legacy check allows sweep|sweep_bulk|library|vault|purge|details, defined at lib/completion-events.ts:5. v2 allows user|system|migration only. Collapsing all six to 'user' destroys the origin surface the completion funnel is measured on. Coordinator ruling requires the origin surface to be preserved, so a new column is needed rather than a lossy collapse.
columns.transform: the legacy six (sweep|sweep_bulk|library|vault|purge|details) are preserved verbatim in origin_surface; the v2 source column records the ACTOR, which is 'user' for all six because all six are user actions. The funnel keeps the surface it is measured on.

columns.name: claimed_at
columns.note: M1:414 requires undone_at >= occurred_at, an ordering the source does NOT enforce (readiness 14.6).

columns.name: undone_at
columns.note: Rows where undone_at < claimed_at exist in the source domain and are rejected by M1:414. They are a reported conflict, never silently swapped or nulled.
columns.conflict: readiness 14.6; probe P07k counts undone_at < claimed_at

columns.name: hours_played
columns.note: double precision hours at the moment of completion. app.completion_events (M1:405-417) has no playtime column at all. readiness 8.2 lists this as the third numeric narrowing and explicitly conditions it on 'if any home is agreed'. Coordinator ruling requires exact minutes to be preserved separately from rounded hours, so if a home is agreed it must be MINUTES with checked rounding and stated provenance, never hours copied across.
columns.transform: the decimal hours are preserved EXACTLY as numeric(30,12) plus the raw source text, with metric_provenance recording that they are legacy authored/derived hours rather than exact observed minutes. Ruling 6 forbids treating an hours mismatch as author attribution and forbids max/coalescing incomparable observations, so no minutes value is synthesised from them.

columns.name: estimate_minutes
columns.note: The duration estimate shown to the user at completion time. Already EXACT MINUTES, so no conversion is needed. No v2 destination exists. Losing it means the funnel can no longer ask whether people complete games that were estimated as short.

columns.name: price_cents
columns.note: Price at the moment of completion, in cents. No v2 destination. catalog_games.price_currency is constrained to USD (readiness 4.12 confirms it), so the currency is unambiguous and the value is a faithful US observation. Losing it means cost-per-hour history cannot be reconstructed, because catalogue prices move.

columns.note: PERSONAL DATA. The reply-to address, NOT NULL. It is the entire point of a contact record and cannot be retired, but it must never appear in a report, a log, a count-only probe result, or any artefact leaving the private boundary. Probes touching this relation return counts only.

columns.note: varchar(150), NOT NULL. User-authored text; may contain personal detail. Nonempty text must not be truncated or dropped.

columns.name: message
columns.note: varchar(5000), NOT NULL. User-authored free text, the most likely place for personal detail in the entire database after `email`. Never truncated, never summarised, never sampled into a report.

columns.name: status
columns.note: smallint workflow state (new, handled, closed). Same code-book requirement as enquiry_type: read from live definitions, never inferred.

columns.name: created_at
columns.note: When the enquiry arrived. Also the key any retention window in D-SUP-2 is measured from.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.note: When it was last actioned. Ordinarily row bookkeeping, but here it is the workflow's own record of handling and is not recoverable from status alone.

columns.note: bigint. The provider's own identifier for the matched game - the key that makes an estimate re-checkable, and the anchor for the known HowLongToBeat AppID-identity mismatch on re-released SKUs, where rescue is by exact normalised title or alias rather than by AppID.

columns.name: next_refresh_at

columns.name: last_error_code

columns.name: created_at
columns.note: When the estimate row was first created.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.note: Row mutation clock; ordinarily a derived-retirement, but unresolved while the relation has no home.

columns.name: evidence
columns.note: jsonb, NOT NULL. The raw provider response that justifies the estimate. Must be treated as OPAQUE TEXT and hashed as text, never re-serialised (readiness 8.5). Before export it must be checked for anything credential-shaped, since it holds provider responses.

relations.name: game_duration_jobs
relations.role: Work queue for duration enrichment, with a lock lease and retry state.
relations.summary: Per plan 14.2 and readiness 14 the queue is NOT a migration destination: in-flight work is not resumed and due work is rebuilt. Root's 11 September durability review added the missing half: current lifecycle state for a catalogued app reaches catalog.provider_state (evidence_kind='duration') and a terminal verdict for an uncatalogued app reaches catalog.appid_terminal_rejections, because migration.legacy_duration_job_archive is staging-30d-post-cutover. lib/duration-worker.ts is the sole writer: 'failed' is the verdict after MAX_ATTEMPTS (line 140-143), 'retry' carries the only record of the effective backoff (line 145), and a 'needs_review' row carries a provider verdict such as duration_not_found or known_title_no_provider_times (line 117-127) that re-running cannot change.
relations.target: catalog.provider_state (mapped AppIDs) + catalog.appid_terminal_rejections (terminal verdicts for uncatalogued AppIDs); the transient queue itself is rebuilt after cutover
relations.archive_purpose: Preserve earned failure history so the rebuilt duration queue does not re-attempt known-bad apps against a provider we are rate-limited by, and so a systematic provider outage remains diagnosable after cutover.
relations.archive_retention: Operational provenance with no account key: retained until the v2 duration pipeline has re-derived its own failure set, reviewed at M7.

retention.bound: until the v2 duration pipeline has re-derived its own failure set
authority: docs/VaultShuffle_v2_architecture_plan.md section 13: shared catalogue evidence and job/worker summaries are bounded operational data with no account key

evidence: readiness 14 (queue relations are design confirmations, not migration conflicts)

columns.name: steam_app_id
columns.note: The app the job was for; kept as the raw appid so an app absent from catalog_games is still recorded.

columns.name: status
columns.note: Archived verbatim AND mapped to durable lifecycle state; 'retry' becomes 'failed' with its fence, which is the only target shape whose CHECK permits a fence, and a needs_review verdict splits into a terminal rejection (duration_not_found / known_title_no_provider_times) or review_required state.

columns.name: priority
columns.note: Retired as scheduling state, not as data.
columns.recoverable_from: Scheduling input for a queue that is rebuilt after cutover from current demand.

columns.name: attempts

columns.name: next_attempt_at

columns.name: last_error_message

columns.name: created_at
columns.note: When the job was queued; gives the failure history an age.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.note: Also catalog.appid_terminal_rejections.last_attempt_at. The job row has no completed/processed instant, so updated_at is the only record of when the last attempt was made.

columns.name: status
columns.note: The 12 September Blacklist product decision changed the terminal-state boundary: current Sleep membership survives as an undated permanent flag until manual Reactivate.

columns.name: hours_played
columns.note: P05 on the verified real snapshot found zero owned-row disagreements with the exact legacy JavaScript rounding path; family rows have unknown personal minutes and are never assigned to the borrower. Exact observed minutes remain runtime authority for owned rows. Legacy hours and raw spelling remain independent evidence and are never maxed, coerced or silently discarded. Final freeze repeats this measurement.

columns.name: completion_percentage
columns.note: Derived at import by inferredCompletionForPayload (lib/game-classification.ts:174) and re-derived on read by gameProgress (:161), with NO provenance flag distinguishing an authored value. Primary rule per readiness 8.4: do NOT populate app.game_state.manual_progress from it, because that would assert authorship the data cannot support. The whole column is retained as evidence so a later provenance decision remains possible.

columns.name: date_added
columns.note: TEXT, not a date, and locale-formatted: lib/steam-owned-games.ts:19 produces it with toLocaleDateString('en-GB'), giving DD/MM/YYYY. lib/validation.ts:29 accepts any trimmed string up to 64 chars, so other formats may exist. Parsing '03/09/2026' with a default or US parser yields March 9, not 3 September. Retained as OPAQUE TEXT with NO date parsing at all, and a documented retirement. Coordinator ruling: retain raw evidence; never parse DD/MM/YYYY with a US or default parser.

columns.name: notes
columns.note: Plan section 2 records zero nonempty notes today, so this is currently a suppression rule rather than a data risk, but the feature is retained and the rule must exist.
columns.transform: Legacy is text NOT NULL and may be ''. v2 requires length(btrim(notes)) between 1 and 10000 (M1:245). Empty and whitespace-only normalise to NULL; the row is then suppressed entirely unless another state field is set, because app.game_state carries a disjunction check (M1:254-259). Nonempty text is NEVER truncated: over-length is a reported conflict.

columns.name: created_at
columns.note: When the library row was created. app.library_games (M1:226-231) deliberately has no timestamps, and app.game_state.updated_at is a mutation clock, not a creation instant. Archived rather than retired because 'when did this game enter my library' is not recoverable from anything else once date_added is retired as unparseable.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.note: Distinct from created_at above, which is archived.
columns.recoverable_from: Row mutation bookkeeping, regenerated by v2 write paths into app.game_state.updated_at. Carries no fact about the user's library.

columns.name: last_observed_played_at

columns.name: recency_source
columns.note: Coordinator ruling: preserve recency provider AND evidence kind as separate facts. This split does that without weakening a frozen constraint.
columns.transform: readiness 4.3: NO legacy value is in the v2 evidence_source list. Legacy allows steam_exact | observed_playtime_change | steam_recent_window (lib/recency.ts:25); v2 evidence_source allows steam_profile | steam_api | user | unknown (M1:269). The two answer DIFFERENT questions: legacy records what KIND of evidence exists, v2 records WHO reported it. evidence_source = 'steam_api' for all three legacy kinds, because all three are Steam-reported, and the KIND is carried EXPLICITLY in app.game_activity.recency_evidence_kind, which the M3 migration adds for this purpose. The earlier proposal encoded the kind in interval nullability; ruling 10 rejects that ('Interval nullability does not necessarily encode the original evidence kind; preserve it explicitly where needed'), and an interval start is never invented.

columns.name: recency_evidence_at
columns.note: M1:275 requires interval_ended_at >= interval_started_at, which a null start satisfies.
columns.transform: The upper bound of the evidence window. interval_started_at stays NULL for observed_playtime_change because legacy genuinely does not record it (readiness 4.3) and inventing a bound would fabricate evidence.

columns.name: observed_playtime_minutes
columns.note: The exact measurement. NULL stays NULL and hours_played = 0 must NEVER become an observed zero - M1:224-225 states the invariant explicitly. This column is the reason exact minutes can be preserved separately from rounded hours. Whether it is the SOLE source is D-LIB-1, blocked on probe P05.

columns.name: family_owner_steam_id
columns.note: readiness 4.8. Plain text with NO foreign key to user_family_members. v2 app.family_game_access (M1:331) requires a composite FK to app.family_members(account_id, id), so any family row whose lender row has since been removed cannot be represented as family access. Coordinator ruling forbids fabricating family access to make rows fit, so the options are (a) drop the access row and archive the evidence, or (b) synthesise a member row, which fabricates access and is therefore rejected.
columns.transform: resolved to the composite FK app.family_game_access(account_id, member_id) by matching app.family_members.steam_id. A row whose lender record no longer exists does NOT get a synthesised member: ruling 8 says orphan family-access evidence is retained privately and does not manufacture a member or confer access, so it lands in migration.legacy_family_access_orphans with its disposition recorded. How many such rows exist is snapshot check S-FAM-ORPHAN.

relations.name: vault_events
relations.role: User actions against a library game from the vault surface, with a free-form jsonb context.
relations.summary: Vault action history is preserved in app.vault_events. context is carried as opaque jsonb and is never re-serialised; its key distribution must be checked for personal data before export.
evidence: readiness 6.3 (vault_events.game_id has a real FK to user_games(id))

columns.name: id
columns.note: Event identity.
columns.transform: uuid -> bigint identity with the legacy uuid retained as public_id.

columns.name: user_id
columns.note: Would resolve through migration.account_map.
columns.transform: legacy uuid -> integer account id through migration.account_map; the legacy uuid is not lost because app.accounts.public_id retains it.

columns.name: game_id
columns.note: A user_games UUID with a real FK (readiness 6.3), so it needs migration.library_row_map. Nullable, so an event with no game is a real state.
columns.transform: legacy user_games uuid -> catalog game id through migration.library_row_map; the source uuid is retained in legacy_game_id so an event whose library row was deleted keeps its referent. NULL stays NULL: an event with no game is a real state.

columns.name: action
columns.note: The action taken. Value domain must be read from live definitions before writing a target constraint.

columns.name: context
columns.note: jsonb, NOT NULL. Must be treated as OPAQUE TEXT and hashed as text, never re-serialised (readiness 8.5). Its contents are unaudited, so before any export it must be checked for personal data rather than assumed safe.

columns.name: created_at
columns.note: Event instant.

constraints.name: vault_events_game_id_fkey
constraints.definition: FOREIGN KEY (game_id) REFERENCES user_games(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

constraints.name: vault_events_user_id_fkey
constraints.definition: FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES app_accounts(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
